why: Caffeine blocks adenosine receptors, so a coffee at 21:00 lowers late-evening drowsiness and delays sleep onset.
source: Drake et al. 2013 J Clin Sleep Med; Clark & Landolt 2017 Sleep Med Rev

why: Caffeine partially restores vigilance and reaction-time performance lost to short sleep.
source: Institute of Medicine 2001 'Caffeine for the Sustainment of Mental Task Performance'; McLellan et al. 2016 Neurosci Biobehav Rev

why: People with anxiety disorders are more sensitive to caffeine's anxiogenic effect.
source: Bruce et al. 1992 Arch Gen Psychiatry; Smith 2002 Food Chem Toxicol

why: Stopping regular caffeine causes fatigue and drowsiness within 12-48 h, even after modest daily intake.
source: Juliano & Griffiths 2004 Psychopharmacology

why: Caffeine withdrawal includes difficulty concentrating.
source: Juliano & Griffiths 2004 Psychopharmacology; DSM-5 caffeine withdrawal criteria

why: Increased appetite is a core nicotine withdrawal symptom and drives post-cessation weight gain.
source: Hughes 2007 Nicotine Tob Res; DSM-5 tobacco withdrawal

why: Irritability, anxiety and restlessness peak in the first days after quitting smoking.
source: Hughes 2007 Nicotine Tob Res; Shiffman et al. 2004

why: The post-binge 'crash' brings dysphoria and anhedonia for days.
source: Gawin & Kleber 1986 Arch Gen Psychiatry; DSM-5 stimulant withdrawal

why: Early stimulant withdrawal features fatigue and hypersomnia.
source: DSM-5 stimulant withdrawal; Morgan & Malison 2007 Sleep Med Clin

why: Stimulants improve attention in ADHD, including in distracting settings.
source: Cortese et al. 2018 Lancet Psychiatry network meta-analysis

why: Appetite suppression is the most common methylphenidate side effect.
source: Storebo et al. 2015 Cochrane Review; Cortese et al. 2018

why: A single SSRI dose does not lift mood; antidepressant benefit needs weeks.
source: Harmer et al. 2009 Br J Psychiatry; standard pharmacology texts

why: After four weeks of an SSRI, depressed mood improves, though the drug-specific gain is modest.
source: Cipriani et al. 2018 Lancet; Taylor et al. 2006 Arch Gen Psychiatry

why: A sub-anaesthetic ketamine infusion produces a rapid antidepressant response visible at 24 h.
source: Zarate et al. 2006 Arch Gen Psychiatry; McGirr et al. 2015 Psychol Med meta-analysis

why: Benzodiazepines blunt subjective anxiety during acute stress.
source: Baldwin et al. 2013 J Psychopharmacol; Pomara et al. 2005

why: Beta-blockade reduces palpitations and tremor, so felt performance anxiety drops modestly.
source: Steenen et al. 2016 J Psychopharmacol systematic review

why: THC stimulates appetite via CB1 receptors ('the munchies').
source: Kirkham 2005; Abel 1971 Nature; dronabinol label

why: CBD is not intoxicating and 25 mg does not alter perception.
source: Schoedel et al. 2018 Epilepsy Behav (abuse potential); WHO ECDD 2018 CBD review

why: Low oral CBD doses have no measurable mood effect in healthy people.
source: Babalonis et al. 2017 Drug Alcohol Depend; Zuardi et al. 2017

why: Low daytime melatonin doses produce mild sleepiness.
source: Dollins et al. 1994 PNAS

why: Semaglutide reduces appetite and energy intake substantially.
source: Blundell et al. 2017 Diabetes Obes Metab; Friedrichsen et al. 2021

why: Oral morphine 10 mg modestly lowers respiratory drive in opioid-naive adults.
source: Dahan et al. 2010 Anesthesiology; Pattinson 2008 Br J Anaesth

why: Sensory over-responsivity in autism makes loud crowded places distressing.
source: Green & Ben-Sasson 2010 J Autism Dev Disord; Ben-Sasson et al. 2009

why: A single exercise bout gives a short-lived mood lift in depressed people.
source: Bartholomew et al. 2005 Med Sci Sports Exerc

why: D2 blockade blunts drive and can cause dysphoria in healthy volunteers.
source: Voruganti & Awad 2004 Psychopharmacology; Artaloytia et al. 2006

why: Attention deficits in ADHD are worse amid distraction.
source: DSM-5; Willcutt et al. 2005 Biol Psychiatry

why: ADHD does not involve altered perception.
source: DSM-5

why: Crowded noisy settings provoke more anxiety in autistic people due to sensory sensitivity.
source: Green & Ben-Sasson 2010; van Steensel et al. 2011 Clin Child Fam Psychol Rev

why: Persistently low mood is a core symptom of major depression.
source: DSM-5

why: Anhedonia and loss of drive are core symptoms of depression.
source: DSM-5; Treadway & Zald 2011 Neurosci Biobehav Rev

why: Depression does not change respiratory drive.
source: Clinical physiology; DSM-5

why: GAD involves persistent excessive worry and tension.
source: DSM-5

why: Chronic stress raises baseline tension and worry.
source: McEwen 2007 Physiol Rev

why: Chronic stress lowers well-being and is a risk factor for depression.
source: Hammen 2005 Annu Rev Clin Psychol; McEwen 2007

why: Five hours a night accumulates sleep pressure and daytime sleepiness.
source: Van Dongen et al. 2003 Sleep; Belenky et al. 2003

why: Chronic sleep restriction progressively degrades sustained attention.
source: Van Dongen et al. 2003 Sleep

why: Sleep restriction lowers positive mood and raises irritability.
source: Dinges et al. 1997 Sleep; Pilcher & Huffcutt 1996 meta-analysis

why: Melatonin rises after ~21:00, peaks in mid-night and is near zero during daylight.
source: Arendt 2005 J Biol Rhythms; Burgess & Fogg 2008

why: ACTH drives the cortisol rhythm and peaks in the early morning.
source: Krieger 1971 J Clin Endocrinol Metab; Chan & Debono 2010

why: Alertness is lowest in the early-morning circadian nadir and high across the day.
source: Dijk & Czeisler 1995 J Neurosci; Monk 2005

why: Sleepiness peaks during the biological night when sleep pressure and circadian drive align.
source: Åkerstedt & Gillberg 1990; Dijk & Czeisler 1995

why: Adenosine builds up during waking and clears during sleep.
source: Porkka-Heiskanen et al. 1997 Science; Landolt 2008

why: Cognitive performance dips to its nadir in the early-morning hours.
source: Blatter & Cajochen 2007 Physiol Behav

why: Cortisol still peaks shortly after waking; the morning rise follows wake time.
source: Leproult et al. 1997 Sleep; Spiegel et al. 1999 Lancet

why: Depression keeps the morning cortisol peak but often with a raised, flatter evening level.
source: Stetler & Miller 2011 Psychosom Med meta-analysis

why: Caffeine's alerting effect grows with dose in this range.
source: Smith 2002 Food Chem Toxicol

why: Psilocybin's perceptual effects are strongly dose-dependent.
source: Hasler et al. 2004 Psychopharmacology; Griffiths et al. 2011

why: Alcohol's impairment of attention scales with blood alcohol.
source: Zoethout et al. 2011 Br J Clin Pharmacol meta-analysis

why: Tolerance to opioid euphoria develops rapidly with daily use.
source: Williams et al. 2013 Pharmacol Rev; Koob & Volkow 2010

why: In habitual users caffeine mostly reverses withdrawal, so the net gain over a never-user is smaller.
source: James & Rogers 2005 Psychopharmacology; Rogers et al. 2013

why: Alcohol adds to opioid respiratory depression and is common in overdose deaths.
source: van der Schrier et al. 2017 Anesthesiology; Darke & Zador 1996 Addiction

why: Benzodiazepines potentiate opioid respiratory depression (FDA boxed warning).
source: FDA 2016 boxed warning on opioid-benzodiazepine co-use; Jones et al. 2012 Drug Alcohol Depend

why: Alcohol and benzodiazepines have additive sedative effects.
source: Linnoila et al. 1990; Tanaka 2002 J Toxicol Clin Toxicol

why: Naloxone displaces opioids from mu receptors and reverses respiratory depression.
source: Boyer 2012 N Engl J Med

why: Cocaine produces marked euphoria, while one coffee changes mood only slightly.
source: Fischman et al. 1976; Smith 2002

why: Caffeine's performance benefit is larger when alertness is low from sleep loss.
source: McLellan et al. 2016 Neurosci Biobehav Rev; Lieberman 2002

why: Anxiety-disorder patients show heightened anxiogenic responses to caffeine.
source: Charney et al. 1985 Arch Gen Psychiatry; Bruce et al. 1992

why: Sensory over-responsivity makes the same environment more stressful for autistic people.
source: Green & Ben-Sasson 2010; Ben-Sasson et al. 2009

why: SSRI mood benefit appears only after weeks, not after a single dose.
source: Taylor et al. 2006 Arch Gen Psychiatry

why: The day-after mood lift from ketamine is seen in depression, not in healthy people.
source: Zarate et al. 2006; Nugent et al. 2019 Neuropsychopharmacology
